newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO MARKET WAITS FOR CASH TO ROLL IN, BUT WHEN?
newsitem.headline: OLO MARKET WAITS FOR CASH TO ROLL IN, BUT WHEN?

text.p: The Belgian OLO market will be flush with cash this week, but dealers were divided on whether the money from annual coupon payments would come their way soon.

Most expected fund managers to hold off investing until the results of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting was out of the way. But the Belgian Treasury's monthly OLO auction today made the picture more complicated.

Some predicted the auction would be a flop, as primary dealers also stood on the sidelines, while others said their would be a scramble for paper in order to sell it on to the newly cash-rich end investors.

The Treasury is due to make coupon payments on four bonds on Friday, March 28, for a total of around 59 billion Belgian francs (Reuter calculation based on outstanding amount in each OLO line), broken down as follows:

OLO 25 (5.00 pct, March 2001) 10.3 billion francs; OLO 6 (9.00 pct, March 2003) 32.3 billion francs; OLO 26 (6.25 pct, March 2007) 12.5 billion francs; OLO 23 (8.00 pct, March 2015) 4.0 billion francs.
In addition the Treasury will have to make coupon payments on the additional amounts it sells in OLO 25 and 26 at today's auction.

In early trade on Monday, linear bonds were higher with Bunds, with the yield on the benchmark OLO 26 maturing 2007 falling to 6.03 percent from 6.07 percent on Friday. But dealers said volume was thin and most of the movement was in prices rather than real trades.

"We don't see any buyers for the moment. They were promising to buy at six percent, but we still don't see them," one trader at a domestic bank said. "In this context I don't see the auction performing very well."
However, Francoise Bernard, market economist at Dexia CC, said she expected a big auction because of the coupon payments.
All players agreed the market had priced in a 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates at Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting. The Fed Funds rate is now at 5.25 percent.
They said the market would, however, remain nervous ahead of the meeting in case the Fed signalled a 50 basis point rise.

One trader said he would welcome a 50 point hike because it would be a clear signal the Fed was acting pre-emptively to kill inflation. "My impression is that a rate hike now would not have the same impact as in 1994," he added, noting the 1994 Fed move caught all markets off guard. -- Nick Antonovics, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6817, Fax +32 2 230 7710
